newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rightist candidates running scared in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Rightist candidates running scared in Paris.

text.p: Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, a longtime ally of President Jacques Chirac and the target of sleaze probes, was forced into a second-round ballot in a parliamentary election in his Paris constituency, officials said on Monday.
The contest was one of several in which French right-wingers found themselves in tight election contests in the capital, a traditional rightist stronghold.
Others pushed into runoffs in Paris constituencies included Gaullist Justice Minister Jacques Toubon and Gaullist former prime minister Edouard Balladur.
Voter surveys showed that a general swing to the left across France was even more pronounced in Paris.
Tiberi, a member of parliament since 1968, won 33.5 percent of the vote to 27.9 percent for Socialist opponent Lyne Cohen-Solal, meaning the two will face off in this Sunday's runoff.
The weak showing reflected voter anger at the mayor over sleaze scandals in the capital. Twenty-eight people ran against Tiberi in his Left Bank district.
He is under judicial investigation over the alleged payment of a fictitious salary to his wife Xaviere by a local authority in the Paris region run by a fellow Gaullist.

Tiberi also was president of the Paris housing authority at a time when Chirac's Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) allegedly received illicit funding through kickbacks on public housing contracts, according to another judicial probe.
Toubon, who is mayor of the capital's 13th district as well as justice minister, won 35 percent of the first-round vote to 29.8 percent for Socialist opponent Serge Blisko.
Balladur polled 49.3 percent to 21.8 percent for Socialist rival Anne Le Moal, forcing him into a runoff.
